ei.title: The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet
ei.subject: 영어2

fullPassage: The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there?” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see.” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle. Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in.” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders. At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation. Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. “The people in charge just couldn’t cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater,” she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean’s surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes. Earle’s residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth’s surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts’ historic moon landing. In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world’s deepest solo dive at that time. It earned her the title “Her Deepness.” As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself. During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong’s first steps on the moon and noted “These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two ‘final frontiers’ yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean.” Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater. Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA’s focus from exploiting the ocean’s resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean’s conservation. Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health. For Earle, Mission Blue represents not only an organization, but also a movement, driven by a shared passion for the ocean and dedication to its preservation. As an oceanographer, author, and lecturer, she consistently inspires individuals to acknowledge the ocean’s significance. Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared. Ten percent of the sharks remain. They are not all gone. However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.” Although humans are largely responsible for many of the stresses on the ocean, Earle believes that we also have the power to ensure its survival. Earle reminds us of the importance of the ocean by saying, “If you think the ocean isn’t important, imagine Earth without it. No ocean, no life.” With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① Having: 'Having moved to Florida'는 「having+과거분사」의 완료 분사구문이라 적절해요.

✅ ② gifted: 'her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles'에서 과거의 일을 나타내는 과거동사라 적절해요.

❌ ③ loving → loved: 'someone who ___ the ocean'에서 밑줄은 주격 관계대명사 who의 동사예요. 관계절에는 정동사가 필요하므로 과거동사 loved가 맞고, loving은 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ④ dive: 'all you have to do is dive in'에서 「do 강조 뒤」에 오는 원형부정사 보어라 적절해요.
det.tip: 관계대명사 who 뒤에는 정동사가 와야 해요: someone who loved the ocean.

❌ ② walking → walked: 'she dove 381 meters deep and ___ on the ocean floor'에서 앞의 과거동사 dove와 and로 나란히 이어지는 병렬 구조예요. 따라서 과거동사 walked가 맞고, walking은 틀려요 ← 정답

✅ ③ marked: 'It was marked as the world's deepest solo dive'에서 be동사 뒤 수동태 과거분사라 적절해요.

✅ ④ flashed: 'the glowing creatures that flashed like stars'에서 관계대명사 that의 과거동사라 적절해요.
det.tip: and로 동사를 이으면 시제·형태를 맞춰요: dove and walked.

det.tip: 국립 해양 대기청 최초의 여성 수석 과학자로 1990년에 임명되었어요.

ch: 그녀는 1990년 국립 해양 대기청 최초의 여성 수석 과학자로 임명되었다.
그녀는 그 기관의 초점을 해양 연구·보존에서 자원 개발로 바꾸려 했다.
정부 고위 관료로서 그녀는 표현과 행동의 자유를 완전히 보장받았다.
그녀는 끝까지 그 기관에 남아 관료로서 활동을 이어갔다.

questions.passage: In 2009, her efforts ①<u>gained</u> prominence through three key events. She played an important role in ②<u>initiating</u> a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that ③<u>grants</u> winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which ④<u>serves</u> as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① gained: 'her efforts gained prominence'에서 과거의 일을 나타내는 과거동사라 적절해요.

✅ ② initiating: 'played an important role in initiating'에서 전치사 in 뒤에 오는 동명사라 적절해요.

✅ ③ grants: 'a distinguished annual award that grants winners'에서 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수 'an award(하나의 상)'라 단수 동사 grants가 적절해요.

❌ ④ serves → serve: 'marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which ___ as refuges'에서 which가 가리키는 것은 복수 'areas(구역들)'예요. 따라서 복수 동사 serve가 맞고, serves는 틀려요 ← 정답
det.tip: 관계대명사 which가 복수 명사(areas)를 받으면 동사도 복수: which serve.

questions.passage: The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean.  When people asked her, “Isn’t it scary down there? ” she would reply, “What’s there to be afraid of?  When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see. ” Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 대부분의 사람들이 우주 탐사에 매료되어 있을 때, 한 놀라운 인물이 남들보다 앞서 진가를 알아본 대상이 무엇인지 본문에서 찾아 (영어로) 쓰시오. (5단어)

det.korean: 정답: the appeal of the ocean (바다의 매력)
det.analysis: 본문 'one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others'에서, 대부분의 사람들이 우주 탐사에 매료되어 있을 때 한 놀라운 인물이 남들보다 먼저 진가를 알아본 대상은 '바다의 매력(the appeal of the ocean)'이에요.
det.tip: appreciated ___ before many others 뒤에 나오는 대상을 찾으면 돼요.

questions.passage: Earle said, “Since the 1980s, about half of the world’s coral reefs have disappeared.  Ten percent of the sharks remain.  They are not all gone.  However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species.  There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm.
questions.stem: 위 글에 따르면, 오늘날 고래와 거북이의 수가 예전보다 더 많은 까닭은 대부분의 국가가 그들에게 무엇을 하고 있기 때문인지, 그 행동을 본문에서 찾아 (영어로) 쓰시오. (4단어)

det.korean: 정답: protecting them from harm (그들을 위험으로부터 보호하기)
det.analysis: 본문 'There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm'에서, 고래와 거북이가 더 많은 까닭은 대부분의 국가가 그들을 '위험으로부터 보호하고 있기(protecting them from harm)' 때문이에요.
det.tip: because most nations are ___ 뒤에 나오는 행동을 찾으면 돼요.

questions.passage: Having __________ (move) to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (영어로) 쓰시오. (1단어)

det.analysis: 구문 분석: 'Having ___ (move) to Florida ..., she began ...'은 「having+과거분사」의 완료 분사구문이에요. 주절의 동작(began)보다 먼저 일어난 일을 나타내므로 move를 과거분사 moved로 바꿔 'Having moved to Florida(플로리다로 이주한 뒤)'가 돼요.
det.tip: having + 과거분사(moved): ~한 뒤에 (완료 분사구문).

questions.passage: She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.  Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey.  Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico.  On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean.  Her father encouraged her, saying, “These will help you with your underwater explorations.  Now all you have to do is dive in. ” With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean’s wonders.  At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend’s father.  Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater.  As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 잠수 장비의 기술 원리는 글의 소재가 아니에요.

✅ ② 글은 전설적인 해양 생물학자 Sylvia Earle이 바다를 탐험하고 지켜 온 삶과 업적을 다뤄요 ← 정답

❌ ③ 멕시코만 해양 생물은 도입부의 배경일 뿐 주제가 아니에요.

❌ ④ 성차별 극복은 일부 사건일 뿐 글 전체의 주제가 아니에요.
det.tip: 제목과 도입부('the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle')가 인물 중심임을 알려 줘요.

ch: 심해 잠수 장비의 기술적 발전 과정과 원리
바다 탐험과 보존에 헌신한 한 전설적인 해양 생물학자의 삶과 업적
플로리다 멕시코만에 서식하는 해양 생물의 생태 특징

questions.passage: Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean’s conservation.  Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean.  In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events.  She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems.  She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support.  Earle’s wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or “Hope Spots,” which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats.  Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean.  Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023.  Mission Blue’s goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s recommended target for maintaining ocean health.
questions.stem: 위 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 그녀는 오히려 제약이 많던 정부직을 떠나 더 활발히 활동했어요.

❌ ② 본문 'protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8%'에서 보호 구역은 늘어났어요.

❌ ③ 강연·집필·사업 등 여러 방식을 함께 활용했지 특정 방식이 더 중요하다고 하지 않았어요.

✅ ④ 강연·집필·디지털 플랫폼·Mission Blue 등 다양한 활동으로 바다 보존의 중요성을 알리고 실천을 이끌었다는 것이 요지예요 ← 정답
det.tip: 요지 = 글쓴이의 핵심 메시지: 다양한 활동으로 바다 보존을 알리고 실천을 이끌다.

ch: 정부 기관에서 일하는 것이 해양 보존에 가장 효과적인 방법이다.
해양 보호 구역은 국제기구의 규제 탓에 오히려 계속 줄어들고 있다.
학술 논문 발표가 대중 강연보다 환경 보호에 훨씬 더 중요하다.
그녀는 다양한 활동과 자신이 세운 비영리 단체를 통해 바다 보존의 중요성을 알리고 실천을 이끌어 왔다.

Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater.  As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Sylvia Earle’s love for the ocean __________.
questions.stem:
위 글의 내용을 바탕으로, 다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 따라 영작하시오.

"바다를 향한 그녀의 사랑은 더 멀리 탐험하고자 하는 열망에 불을 지폈다."

[조건]

det.korean: 정답: fueled her desire to explore further
det.analysis:
구문 분석:

- 수식: to explore further(더 멀리 탐험하려는)가 desire를 뒤에서 꾸며요.
- 그래서 'fueled her desire to explore further' 순서가 돼요.
